headline: Highest risk is Open Interpreter’s broad filesystem/code execution interacting with whisper’s file-based audio ingestion, creating medium prompt-injection and data-leakage exposure; no direct capability conflict or compliance mismatch is…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter can read/write the user filesystem and parse clipboard/stdin content, while whisper consumes audio files only. A malicious transcript or file placed on shared storage could be treated as instructions by Open Interpreter if the operator bridges outputs manually or via files. whisper itself does not execute instructions, so the risk is interaction-driven, not intrinsic.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter ingests text derived from whisper outputs or shared files as instructions
IF the operator copies whisper-transcribed content into Open Interpreter without review
mitigations: Disable clipboard/file-based handoff between the agents
Review transcribed text before passing it to Open Interpreter
Keep whisper outputs in a separate directory with read-only permissions
Run Open Interpreter in confirmation-required mode, not --auto_run
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter has broad filesystem access and can handle model-provider API keys; whisper reads audio files but has no network egress. If both touch the same local workspace, sensitive audio or transcripts can be exposed to Open Interpreter’s broader context. whisper does not upload data itself, so the leak path is local rather than third-party exfiltration.
conditions: IF audio files or transcripts are stored in a shared local workspace
IF Open Interpreter is pointed at directories containing sensitive recordings
mitigations: Store audio inputs in a dedicated restricted folder
Delete transcripts after use
Limit Open Interpreter to a narrow working directory
Avoid placing secrets in filenames or adjacent notes
requires-engineering: isolate the agents in separate OS users or containers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter can write the filesystem and modify git state; whisper cannot write, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. The pair therefore lacks overlapping write authority, so direct conflict is limited. Any contention would come from the orchestrator or shared files, not from whisper’s own capabilities.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives whisper write access not shown in its profile
IF both agents are manually pointed at the same mutable directory
mitigations: Keep whisper read-only
Use separate output directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same git repo
Serialize any file moves or renames
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared workspaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: Open Interpreter can act on text it receives, and whisper produces transcripts that may be treated as authoritative by an operator or downstream script. If transcript errors are not checked, Open Interpreter may execute incorrect commands or edits based on them. whisper does not verify its own outputs, so the cascade is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF whisper transcripts are used as direct input to Open Interpreter
IF no human or automated verification step checks transcript accuracy
mitigations: Require human review before acting on transcripts
Use confidence thresholds before forwarding text
Keep Open Interpreter in confirmation mode
Annotate transcripts with source audio references
requires-engineering: add automated validation against the original audio

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. Open Interpreter handles local machine data and whisper handles audio files; the profiles do not show a compliance conflict such as PHI or EU PII crossing jurisdictions. Because the evidence is sparse, this is a low-confidence, low-severity compliance assessment rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through either agent without an external policy review
IF local audio files contain data subject to special retention rules
mitigations: Classify audio before processing
Avoid regulated data in transcripts
Document retention for generated text files
Restrict access to local workspaces
requires-engineering: add jurisdiction-aware routing and retention controls
